title: the WSG land-based animals - Table 13 (the animal encumbrance limits and movement rates)
audit_comment: The land-based animals slice pins Table 13 (the 18 mounts and beasts of burden x the normal and maximum loads and the unencumbered/encumbered rates over the three terrain classes), the forced-move stamina rules (the half-rate hour cap, the cumulative fatigue chances) and the accelerated no-rest spillover (rules/wsganimal.h, prefix wam); census 357 -> 358.

banner.title: The WSG LAND-BASED ANIMALS, R433: Table 13 (the encumbrance limits and movement rates for animals - the 18 rows from the ape to the yak x the normal load, the maximum load and the unencumbered/encumbered movement rates over normal, rugged and very rugged terrain) with the two-designation rules (the normal load is unencumbered, the maximum load still moves), the forced-move stamina rules (the hours equal half the rate, capped at 12; the cumulative fatigue chance 20/35/50 percent by terrain; the book own light and medium warhorse examples) and the accelerated no-rest +1/3 spillover from the Table 12 section (16 + 5 = 21) - the round continues the encumbrance-and-movement chapter. Census 357 -> 358.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed pp. 31-32; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (16 of 18 rows) and the IIIF full-resolution eye-reads (the Sheep and Yak rows and the light-war very-rugged cell, absent from the djvu text layer, read 250/500 9/6 6/3 6/3, 2250/3500 12/6 9/6 6/3 and 6/3 at full resolution); every number matched. The camel footnote markers point forward to the Mounts and Beasts of Burden section (out of this slice).
banner.sentinel: The Table 13 movement columns read unencumbered/encumbered: the left figure applies at the normal load or less, the right figure when encumbered (over the normal load up to the maximum); a 0 means the animal cannot move or be moved into that terrain under that encumbrance. The forced-move hours are the current rate over 2, up to 12; past that the fatigue chance is cumulative per hour.

consts.name: wamForcedHoursDen
consts.comment: An animal can be forced to move for hours equal to half its current movement rate (the denominator).

consts.name: wamForcedHoursMax
consts.comment: The forced-move window caps at 12 hours.

consts.name: wamFatNormPct
consts.comment: The cumulative fatigue chance per hour past the window, normal terrain.

consts.name: wamFatRugPct
consts.comment: The cumulative fatigue chance per hour, rugged terrain.

consts.name: wamFatVrPct
consts.comment: The cumulative fatigue chance per hour, very rugged terrain.

consts.name: wamAccelNorestNum
consts.comment: Keeping the accelerated pace without the rest stops adds 1/3 of the given amount (numerator).

consts.name: wamAccelNorestDen
consts.comment: The accelerated no-rest denominator (rounded to the nearest whole).

bools.name: wamCharCategoriesDontApply
bools.comment: The character encumbrance categories do not apply to mounts and pack animals.

bools.name: wamTwoDesignationsOnly
bools.comment: Only two designations matter for an animal: the normal load and the maximum load.

bools.name: wamNormalLoadUnencumbered
bools.comment: The normal load is what an animal carries without being encumbered.

bools.name: wamMaxLoadStillMoves
bools.comment: The maximum load is the greatest encumbrance the animal can carry and still be able or willing to move.

bools.name: wamRateVariesWithTerrain
bools.comment: An animal's large-scale rate varies with terrain, as a character's does.

bools.name: wamRateIndicatesStamina
bools.comment: The rate of a mount or beast of burden also indicates its stamina.

bools.name: wamFatigueCumulative
bools.comment: The fatigue chance past the forced-move window is cumulative per hour.

bools.name: wamLeftIsUnencumbered
bools.comment: The left figure of a slash pair is the rate at the normal load or less.

bools.name: wamRightIsEncumbered
bools.comment: The right figure of a slash pair is the rate when encumbered, over the normal load up to the maximum.

bools.name: wamZeroCannotMove
bools.comment: A 0 entry means the animal cannot move or be moved into that terrain under that encumbrance.

bools.name: wamTableNotExhaustive
bools.comment: The table does not include every conceivable animal; an animal friendship or charm spell can work wonders.

bools.name: wamDmComparesSimilarBeast
bools.comment: For a new animal the DM weighs its size, strength and rate and compares it to a similar listed beast (the tiger vs the yak).

examples.note: the light warhorse, unencumbered, normal terrain: rate 24
the forced-move window: 24 over 2 = 12 hours without adverse effects
at the end of 13 hours: a 20 percent chance of fatigue
after 14 hours: the chance rises to 40 percent
the medium warhorse, encumbered, rugged terrain: rate 6
the forced-move window: 6 over 2 = three consecutive hours without incident
at the end of four hours: a 35 percent chance of fatigue
after five hours: the chance rises to 70 percent
six hours: a 105 percent chance - fatigue is automatic

examples.expr: 2 * 16 * m['wamAccelNorestNum']() - 2 * 5 * m['wamAccelNorestDen']() < -m['wamAccelNorestDen']() or 2 * 16 * m['wamAccelNorestNum']() - 2 * 5 * m['wamAccelNorestDen']() > m['wamAccelNorestDen']()
examples.note: the accelerated pace kept up without the rest stops: 16 + 5 = 21 (the +1/3 of 16 rounded to the nearest whole is 5 - written division-free, the rounding inequality)
the tiger comparison: the yak normal load is 2250 gp
